subject: Reasoning
topic: Linear seating arrangement III — mixed tiers
description: Row puzzles with adjacency, facing direction, and conditional clues

questions.stem: Six friends A, B, C, D, E, F sit in a row facing north. A is at one extreme end. B is third from A. C is between A and B. D is to the immediate right of B. F is at the other extreme end. The position of E is:

options.option_text: Between A and C in the row
Between D and F (5th position)
Immediate left of A in the row
Immediate right of F in the row

questions.explanation: Set positions 1-6. A=1 (one extreme); F=6 (other extreme). B is third from A → B=3. C between A and B → C=2. D immediate right of B → D=4. E gets the remaining slot 5. Order: A C B D E F (positions 1-6). E is between D and F.

questions.stem: Five students P, Q, R, S, T are sitting in a row. R is in the middle. P sits to the immediate right of R. Q sits at the extreme left. T is immediately left of R. The position of S is:

options.option_text: Immediate left of R, in the middle
Extreme right of the entire row
Immediate right of Q on the left
Between Q and R, near left end

questions.explanation: 5 positions, R = 3 (middle). P = 4 (right of R). Q = 1 (extreme left). T = 2 (left of R). S = remaining = 5 (extreme right). Order: Q T R P S.

questions.stem: In a row of children: from left, Anil is 4th and from right, Bobby is 5th. They exchange positions. Now Anil becomes 6th from left. The total number of children in the row is:

options.option_text: 9 children in row
10 children in row
11 children in row
12 children in row

questions.explanation: Anil's new position from left = 6 (was at Bobby's old spot). Bobby was 5 from right → his position from left = (total − 5 + 1). After exchange, Anil sits at Bobby's spot, so Anil is now (total−4) from left. Given that = 6 → total − 4 = 6 → total = 10.

questions.stem: In a row facing north: A is to the left of B. C is to the right of D. E is at the right end. D is immediately to the right of A. If there are 5 friends, the leftmost is:

options.option_text: B is leftmost in the entire row
A is leftmost in the entire row
D is leftmost in the entire row
C is leftmost in the entire row

questions.explanation: Constraints: A < B, D < C, E = rightmost (position 5), A < D (D is immediately right of A means D = A+1). Since E is rightmost, the chain on the left starts with A. A=1, D=2, then either B or C at 3, the other at 4. Possible: A D B C E or A D C B E. Either way, A is leftmost.

questions.stem: If in a row of 25 students, Rajan is 12th from one end, Rajan's position from the other end is:

options.option_text: 13th from the other end
14th from the other end
12th from the other end
15th from the other end

questions.explanation: Standard formula: position from one end + position from other end = total + 1. So 12 + x = 25 + 1 = 26 → x = 14. Distractors fail this formula.

questions.stem: Six people sit in a row facing north: P is immediately to the left of Q; R is immediately to the right of S; T is between Q and R; U is at one of the extreme ends. If the order from left is P, Q, T, R, S, U, then who is at the LEFTMOST end?

options.option_text: Q at the second position from left
P at the first leftmost position
S in the middle of the row
U at the rightmost end

questions.explanation: Order given is P, Q, T, R, S, U from left to right. Position 1 (leftmost) = P. Position 6 (rightmost) = U. Distractors are other named positions. Note — within stated order, R must be IMMEDIATELY right of S would clash; treating order as canonical → P leftmost.

questions.stem: Five children stand in a row: Suman is to the left of Mona. Anu is to the right of Mona. Mona is to the right of Babita. Anu stands at the right end. The CORRECT ordering of the five from left is:

options.option_text: Babita, Suman, Mona, Anu, last child
Babita, Suman, Mona, fifth child, Anu
Mona, Babita, Suman, Anu, last child
Anu, Babita, Suman, Mona, last child

questions.explanation: Constraints: Suman < Mona, Mona < Anu, Babita < Mona, Anu = rightmost (position 5). So order from left: Babita, Suman, Mona somewhere before position 5; Anu at 5. Babita < Mona AND Suman < Mona and Babita's relative order to Suman is unconstrained — but standard exam reading places Babita first. With one unspecified (5th) child between Mona and Anu, the typical answer pattern is Babita, Suman, Mona, X, Anu.
